statement: Immutable Run 101-simulate scores 49.1905 average dram-device-equivalent WIP, contributing -73.78575 to the Objective; burn-in-1.package-input leads at 9.465692 equivalents and packaging-1.die-input follows at 6.874125. The run-qualified Factory views show packaging-1 processing one die every 1.5 seconds at 60.0% utilization after 96.0 seconds of input wait, while burn-in-1 is a shared fixed-eight-device rack at 68.3% utilization with 76.0 seconds idle, three changeovers totaling 14.0 seconds, and 7.5-second commercial versus 18.75-second performance jobs. Event evidence shows 96 packaging starts but only eleven burn-in batches delivering 88 devices, leaving exactly eight packaged devices at the burn-in input. This is a release/output-quantum and back-end service-cadence observation, not proof that either buffer capacity or all ranked WIP is avoidable. The retained tighter-CONWIP review already proves that suppressing releases can reduce some exposure while failing on-time service; the fixed four-device Process portfolio is likewise prior bounded negative evidence rather than a proposal to rename.
